declarations.description:
A measurement inside a known range — storage used, a plan's quota, a password's strength — drawn as a bar with
its label and value above it. Unlike `c2-progress` it is not a task moving towards done: it has `min` and `max`, and
the native `<meter>` thresholds `low`, `high` and `optimum` judge the value as optimum, sub-optimum or critical,
which colours the bar (and is exposed as the `:state(optimum)`, `:state(suboptimum)` and `:state(critical)` custom
states for styling around it). Give it `segments` instead of a `value` to split the bar into parts, such as
photos, documents and mail in a storage quota, with a legend underneath. A segmented meter with `overage` may pass
`max`, as seats assigned past a licence's limit do: the part past `max` is drawn as an overage segment after a limit
mark, listed in the legend and announced, and the host matches `:state(overage)`.

The value shows as a percentage of the range in the page's language; `value-text` replaces it with your own words
("12.4 GB of 15 GB"), which are also what a screen reader announces, and the `value` slot replaces only what is
shown. A segmented meter shows and announces its total against `max`, and reads each segment out by name.

members.description: The measurement, between `min` and `max`. Ignored when `segments` are set.

members.name: min
members.description: Lower end of the range.

members.name: max
members.description: Upper end of the range.

members.name: low
members.description: Upper end of the low region, as in the native `<meter>`.

members.name: high
members.description: Lower end of the high region, as in the native `<meter>`.

members.name: optimum
members.description:
The best value. Below `low` it makes low values optimum and high ones critical (a fuel gauge reads the other
way: `optimum` above `high`); between them the middle region is optimum and both ends sub-optimum.

members.name: segments
members.description: Parts of a segmented meter, `{ label, value, color? }`, in range units. Accepts a JSON string as an attribute.

members.name: overage
members.description:
Lets a segmented meter pass `max`. Its bar then spans up to the segments' sum, the part past `max` is drawn as an
overage segment after a limit mark, and the shown and announced total is the real sum ("56 of 50"). Without it a
sum past `max` is cut at the end of the track. A single-value meter is always clamped.

members.name: label
members.description: Label when the default slot is empty.

members.name: valueText
members.description: Words for the value ("12.4 GB of 15 GB"), shown and announced in place of the percentage or the total.

members.name: range
members.description: Lower and upper end of the range, with a `max` below `min` treated as equal to it.

members.name: raw
members.description: `value`, or the segments' sum counted from `min`, before clamping.

members.name: current
members.description: The value the bar and the tone use: `value`, or the segments' sum, clamped to the range.

members.name: excess
members.description: How far the segments' sum passes `max` in a segmented meter with `overage`; 0 otherwise.

members.name: tone
members.description: How good the current value is, judged from `low`, `high` and `optimum` the way the native `<meter>` does.

members.name: shownValue
members.description:
The value as shown: `value-text`, the segments' sum against the size of the range (both counted from `min`, like
the legend), or the percentage of the range.

members.name: entries
members.description: The segments as the legend lists them: with the overage after them while there is one.

members.name: announcedValue
members.description: What a screen reader hears: the shown value, after each segment (and the overage) by name in a segmented meter.

declarations.description:
One value placed on a banded scale: a lab result against its reference ranges, a salary inside its pay band, a
PHQ-9 or BMI score against its categories. The bands are drawn side by side along a track with their labels under
them and the numbers where they meet; a pointer marks the value, and the label of the band it falls in shows beside
the value. A value outside `min`–`max` pins the pointer to that end as an arrow pointing off the scale, and still
counts in the first or last band.

A band's `tone` (`optimum`, `suboptimum`, `critical`, as in `c2-meter`) colours it, and while the value is in it the
host matches `:state(<tone>)`; `:state(below-scale)` and `:state(above-scale)` say the value is off the scale.

It is announced as a meter through its own semantics: its label as the name, and the shown value followed by the
band's label as the value.

members.description: End of the scale.

members.name: bands
members.description:
The bands, `{ label, from?, to?, tone?, color? }` in scale units, in order along the scale. Each starts where the
one before it ends unless it sets `from`; the scale shows its track where no band is. Accepts a JSON string as an
attribute.

members.name: valueText
members.description: Words for the value ("112 mg/dL"), shown and announced in place of the number.

members.name: labelObserver
members.description: Redraws when the label's text changes in place, which fires no `slotchange`, so the host's name follows it.

members.name: range
members.description: Start and end of the scale, with a `max` below `min` treated as equal to it.

members.name: resolved
members.description: The bands placed on the scale, clamped to it; empty bands are left out.

members.name: band
members.description: The band the value falls in, a value off the scale counting in the band at that end; undefined between bands.

members.name: placed
members.description: The value on the scale: `value` clamped to `min`–`max`.

members.name: offScale
members.description: Which end of the scale the value is past, if any.
